meaning.en: Fortunes change over time; those who are on top today may be down tomorrow.
meaning.zh: 运气和境遇会变化，今天得势的人明天可能失势。

examples.zh: 风水轮流转，今年终于轮到我们队夺冠了。
examples.en: Fortune turns; this year it was finally our team's turn to win.

examples.zh: 别太得意，风水轮流转，谁也不会一直走运。
examples.en: Don't get cocky; fortunes change and nobody stays lucky for ever.

examples.zh: 他当年被人看不起，如今风水轮流转，成了大老板。
examples.en: He was looked down on back then; now the tables have turned and he's a big boss.

usage.en: Casual, often a warning or consolation. Usually quoted in full, sometimes with 三十年河东，三十年河西.
usage.zh: 口语，常作劝诫或安慰；多完整引用，有时接“三十年河东，三十年河西”。

synonyms: 三十年河东，三十年河西

natural: cannot be put on the table

meaning.en: Not good or respectable enough to be shown in public or taken seriously.
meaning.zh: 不够体面、拿不出手，不能公开示人或被正式对待。

examples.zh: 这种小把戏上不了台面。
examples.en: Such cheap tricks are not fit to be shown in public.

examples.zh: 他的作品粗糙，实在上不了台面。
examples.en: His work is crude and really not fit to be shown.

examples.zh: 私下的玩笑话上不了台面，别在会上说。
examples.en: Private jokes aren't suitable for the table, so don't say them at the meeting.

usage.en: Casual, mildly dismissive; a variant 上不得台面 is also heard.
usage.zh: 口语，略带轻视；也说“上不得台面”。

natural: step into the hall of refinement

meaning.en: To be accepted as elegant and fit for formal or cultured settings.
meaning.zh: 进入高雅正式的场合，被认为够得上雅致。

examples.zh: 民间小调想登大雅之堂，还得提高制作水准。
examples.en: For folk tunes to gain respectability, production standards must improve.

examples.zh: 漫画如今也能登大雅之堂了，还进了美术馆。
examples.en: Comics can now enter polite society, even the art gallery.

examples.zh: 这道家常菜竟也能登大雅之堂，成了国宴菜。
examples.en: This home-style dish has even become respectable enough for a state banquet.

usage.en: Mostly seen in the negative 难登大雅之堂 / 登不了大雅之堂; the positive form says something has gained respectability.
usage.zh: 多见于否定式“难登大雅之堂”“登不了大雅之堂”；肯定式表示获得认可。

natural: eat the smoke and fire of the human world

meaning.en: To live an ordinary life like everyone else, eating cooked food and facing everyday concerns.
meaning.zh: 像普通人一样过着吃饭生活的凡俗日子。

examples.zh: 她虽然是明星，也要食人间烟火，也会为房租发愁。
examples.en: Star though she is, she lives in the real world and worries about rent.

examples.zh: 神仙不食人间烟火，我们凡人可不行。
examples.en: Immortals needn't eat mortal fare, but we ordinary people must.

examples.zh: 这位大学者其实很爱食人间烟火，爱逛菜市场。
examples.en: The great scholar is quite down-to-earth and loves visiting the food market.

usage.en: Mostly seen in the negative 不食人间烟火; the affirmative is a playful counterpart.
usage.zh: 多见于否定式“不食人间烟火”；肯定式是风趣的反用。

natural: the law does not flatter the noble

meaning.en: The law does not bend for the powerful; everyone is equal before it.
meaning.zh: 法律不偏袒权贵，对谁都一视同仁。

equivalents: no one is above the law

examples.zh: 法不阿贵，再高的职位也不能例外。
examples.en: The law favours no one; even the highest office is no exception.

examples.zh: 法院依法审理，体现了法不阿贵的原则。
examples.en: The court tried the case by law, showing that nobody is above it.

examples.zh: 他一向法不阿贵，铁面无私。
examples.en: He has always applied the law without fear or favour.

story.en: Han Fei argued for strict, impartial law: 'The law does not flatter the noble, as the plumb line does not bend for the crooked' (法不阿贵，绳不挠曲).
story.zh: 韩非主张严明执法：“法不阿贵，绳不挠曲。”

usage.en: Usually quoted with 绳不挠曲. Formal; praises impartial justice.
usage.zh: 常与“绳不挠曲”连用，语体庄重，赞扬执法公正。

meaning.en: Belittling something one cannot have in order to soothe one's own disappointment.
meaning.zh: 得不到某样东西，就贬低它来安慰自己的心理。

examples.zh: 他说那家公司不好，其实是酸葡萄心理，因为没被录用。
examples.en: He says that company is bad, but it is sour grapes; they didn't hire him.

examples.zh: 落选后说职位没意思，难免有酸葡萄心理。
examples.en: Saying the post was dull after losing out is plain sour grapes.

examples.zh: 别用酸葡萄心理看待别人的成功。
examples.en: Don't view others' success with a sour-grapes attitude.

usage.en: Modelled on Aesop's fox and the grapes (also known in Chinese as 吃不到葡萄说葡萄酸); a term of popular psychology, used critically.
usage.zh: 出自伊索寓言狐狸与葡萄的故事（汉语也说“吃不到葡萄说葡萄酸”）；是通俗心理学术语，多含批评。

meaning.en: To speak honestly and stick to the facts, neither exaggerating nor playing down.
meaning.zh: 实事求是，有什么就说什么，不夸大也不缩小。

examples.zh: 有一说一，这次是我们做得不够好。
examples.en: To be fair, we did not do well this time.

examples.zh: 我这人有一说一，不会拐弯抹角。
examples.en: I tell it as it is; I don't beat about the bush.

examples.zh: 有一说一，他的方案确实比我的好。
examples.en: Honestly, his proposal really is better than mine.

usage.en: Casual and very common in recent speech, often as a preface to an honest remark.
usage.zh: 口语，近年很常用，常作坦率评论的开场。

meaning.en: To burst onto the scene with great impact, like something from nowhere.
meaning.zh: 形容人或事物突然出现，气势非凡，影响很大。

examples.zh: 这款新手机横空出世，立刻引发抢购。
examples.en: This new phone burst onto the market and caused a buying frenzy.

examples.zh: 一位年轻棋手横空出世，击败了所有对手。
examples.en: A young chess player appeared from nowhere and beat all his rivals.

examples.zh: 这部电影横空出世，颠覆了人们对国产动画的印象。
examples.en: The film exploded onto the scene, changing impressions of domestic animation.

usage.en: Predicate; often in news and reviews. The phrase comes from Mao Zedong's poem 《念奴娇·昆仑》, though here it is simply a modern idiom.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常见于新闻和评论。语出毛泽东《念奴娇·昆仑》“横空出世，莽昆仑”，今作一般成语使用。

meaning.en: Not significant or developed enough to matter; unlikely to amount to anything.
meaning.zh: 成不了大事，没有什么发展前途或影响。

examples.zh: 这些小作坊不成气候，不必担心。
examples.en: These small workshops won't amount to much, so no need to worry.

examples.zh: 他开的小店不成气候，撑不了多久。
examples.en: Their organisation is going nowhere, so there's no need to worry.

examples.zh: 早期的互联网公司大多不成气候。
examples.en: Most early internet firms never amounted to anything.

usage.en: Predicate; also 成不了气候 / 成气候 as a positive.
usage.zh: 多作谓语；也可说“成不了气候”，肯定式为“成气候”。

meaning.en: To make up for a mistake or offence by one's achievements.
meaning.zh: 用功劳来抵消过失或罪过。

equivalents: make up for one's faults by merit

examples.zh: 他立下大功，请求以功抵过。
examples.en: He rendered great service and asked to have it offset his fault.

examples.zh: 功是功，过是过，不能简单地以功抵过。
examples.en: Merit is merit and fault is fault; one cannot simply cancel the other.

examples.zh: 官员想以功抵过，法院并未采纳。
examples.en: The official hoped his achievements would cancel out his offence, but the court did not accept this.

usage.en: Predicate; formal, often in discipline and legal contexts. Often debated, because credit and blame are held separate.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，书面语，常见于纪律和司法语境；功过是否相抵常有争议。

meaning.en: When friends or a couple quarrel, try to reconcile them rather than urge them to split.
meaning.zh: 别人闹矛盾，尤其是夫妻吵架，应该劝他们和好，而不是劝他们分开。

equivalents: be a peacemaker, not a divider

examples.zh: 劝和不劝离，朋友吵架了我们先劝劝。
examples.en: We urge peace, not parting; when friends quarrel we should first try to calm things down.

examples.zh: 老话说劝和不劝离，别随便劝人离婚。
examples.en: The old saying goes: urge reconciliation, not divorce, so don't casually advise a split.

examples.zh: 奶奶坚持劝和不劝离，帮邻居调解了多年。
examples.en: Grandma has always urged reconciliation and spent years mediating for neighbours.

usage.en: Common folk advice, often quoted with 宁拆十座庙，不毁一桩婚. Note that it is a rule of thumb, not meant for abusive relationships.
usage.zh: 民间常用的劝诫，常与“宁拆十座庙，不毁一桩婚”并提；是一般经验，不适用于存在暴力的婚姻。

synonyms: 宁拆十座庙，不毁一桩婚

pinyin: dì qiú lí le shéi dōu zhuàn
natural: the Earth keeps turning without anyone

meaning.en: No one is indispensable; things go on without any one person.
meaning.zh: 没有谁是不可缺少的，少了谁事情都照样进行。

examples.zh: 别觉得自己多重要，地球离了谁都转。
examples.en: Don't think too highly of yourself; the world goes on without anyone.

examples.zh: 他辞职后公司照常运转，地球离了谁都转。
examples.en: The firm ran as usual after he resigned; nobody is indispensable.

examples.zh: 分手没什么大不了，地球离了谁都转。
examples.en: A break-up isn't the end of the world; life goes on.

usage.en: Casual; may be a humble reminder, a consolation, or a snub.
usage.zh: 口语，可以是谦逊的提醒、安慰，也可能是冷言冷语。

synonyms: 死了张屠夫，不吃混毛猪

natural: he who kills must pay with his life

meaning.en: A killer must pay for the crime with his own life.
meaning.zh: 杀了人就应该用自己的性命来抵偿。

examples.zh: 杀人偿命，欠债还钱，是天经地义的事。
examples.en: A killer pays with his life and a debtor pays what he owes; this is only natural.

examples.zh: 古代法律讲究杀人偿命。
examples.en: Ancient law held that a killer must pay with his life.

examples.zh: 受害者家属要求杀人偿命。
examples.en: The victim's family demanded a life for a life.

usage.en: Often paired with 欠债还钱. Reflects traditional views on justice; capital punishment is debated today.
usage.zh: 常与“欠债还钱”并提，反映传统的公正观；今天对死刑仍有争议。

natural: when choosing a wife, choose virtue

meaning.en: In choosing a spouse, character matters more than looks.
meaning.zh: 选择妻子（配偶）要看品德，而不是容貌。

equivalents: character over looks in a partner

examples.zh: 娶妻娶德，不要只看外貌。
examples.en: Choose a wife for virtue and not only for looks.

examples.zh: 奶奶常说娶妻娶德，嫁人嫁品。
examples.en: Grandma often says: marry for virtue, and choose a husband for character.

examples.zh: 他听了老人的话，娶妻娶德，选了个贤惠的姑娘。
examples.en: He took the old man's advice and chose a kind-hearted girl for her virtue.

usage.en: Often quoted in full as 娶妻娶德，嫁人嫁品; traditional wording that a modern speaker may apply to either partner.
usage.zh: 常说全“娶妻娶德，嫁人嫁品”；是传统说法，今天也可用于任何一方。

natural: step back and seek the second best

meaning.en: To settle for the next best option when the first choice is out of reach.
meaning.zh: 得不到最好的，就退一步选择次一等的。

examples.zh: 买不起市中心的房子，只好退而求其次，选了郊区。
examples.en: Unable to afford a place downtown, they settled for the suburbs.

examples.zh: 没拿到冠军，他退而求其次，争取进前三。
examples.en: He failed to take the title and settled for a top-three finish.

examples.zh: 这家店关门了，我们退而求其次，去隔壁吃。
examples.en: That place is closed, so we'll make do with the one next door.

usage.en: Predicate or adverbial; neutral, sometimes mildly regretful.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、状语，中性，有时略带遗憾。

meaning.en: The death of a beautiful woman or the loss of a precious person.
meaning.zh: 美丽的女子或珍贵的人不幸去世。

equivalents: the death of a loved one

examples.zh: 听说她玉碎珠沉，读者无不惋惜。
examples.en: On hearing that she had died, the readers all mourned her.

examples.zh: 小说结尾，女主人公玉碎珠沉，令人心碎。
examples.en: At the end of the novel the heroine dies, breaking the reader's heart.

examples.zh: 诗中以玉碎珠沉哀悼早逝的佳人。
examples.en: The poem uses this image to mourn a beauty dead too young.

usage.en: Literary elegiac phrase, used of young women; rare in modern speech.
usage.zh: 书面挽惜之词，多指年轻女子，现代口语少用。
